title: Mixed Methods at Work
intro: Admins say reporting is essential; the dashboard says almost nobody used it last month. Before choosing a side, check what the data actually counts.

learn.title: Separate observation from explanation
learn.text:
“Few reports were run last month” is **recorded behaviour**.

“Users don't need reporting” is an **explanation** that nobody has established.

The hypothetical: an employee-training platform where admins export completion records. Interviews say the report matters; the analytics show tiny monthly usage; the PM asks whether to keep investing.

try.q: “Users don't need reporting” — what kind of statement is that?
options: A direct quote from the research
try.explain: The data shows usage, not need.

learn.title: Audit the analytics before trusting them
learn.text:
Three questions before accepting the metric:

• **Right users?** Who does the dashboard actually count?
• **Right event?** What does that event record — opening the page, or completing an export?
• **Right window?** A monthly view misses a quarterly task.

In the example the pattern was quarterly: the monthly dashboard made a normal rhythm look like abandonment.

try.q: A task is done once a quarter but the dashboard shows monthly usage. What does the metric look like?
try.explain: The window has to fit the work.

right.label: The audit found
items: Wrong window for a quarterly task

learn.title: Then watch the work
learn.text:
Walking through the **last real attempt** with an admin showed where the time actually went: cleaning up the export afterwards.

The recommendation changed from “deprioritise reporting” to “fix the export clean-up”.

Neither “users said it matters” nor “monthly usage is low” supported a decision on its own.

try.q: What did the triangulated answer turn out to be?
try.explain: The friction was after the export, not in the decision to use it.

test.q: What is the first step when qual and quant disagree?
options: Clarify what the PM is deciding
test.explain: The decision tells you which contradiction matters.

test.q: Which audit question is about the event definition?
options: What does the event actually record?
Does the window fit the work?
How far back does the data go?
test.explain: Opening a page is not completing an export.

test.q: Why walk through the last real attempt?
options: It shows where the time actually goes
It confirms the sample is representative
test.explain: That is how the clean-up problem surfaced.

options: Cutting a feature that was working as intended
The relationship with the admin users
The ability to measure adoption later
test.explain: The usage pattern was normal for a quarterly task.

test.q: What does the article say about choosing a side?
options: Neither source supported a decision alone
Both were wrong about the feature
test.explain: Triangulation produced a different, better answer.
